proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 1
proposals.reason: Section 1 is a definitions section. The clearest study split is by the target's agricultural land, association, and agricultural operation definitions, while repealed entries are not used as study focuses.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Agricultural land definition

evidenceText: land being used in an agricultural operation
land that is not being used in an agricultural operation

proposedGroups.reason: This definition identifies both land currently used in an agricultural operation and land suitable for such use under regulatory criteria.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the two ways land can fall within the agricultural land definition.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Agricultural land owners association definition

evidenceText: an agricultural land owners association incorporated under section 3

proposedGroups.reason: This definition identifies the incorporated association used throughout the Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that an agricultural land owners association is one incorporated under section 3.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Agricultural operation definition

evidenceText: carried on for gain or reward or in the hope or expectation of gain or reward
the clearing, draining, irrigating or cultivation of land
the raising of livestock, including poultry
the production of eggs and milk

proposedGroups.reason: The agricultural operation definition is a large list of activities tied to gain or expected gain.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the gain-or-reward requirement and listed activities that can be an agricultural operation.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 2
proposals.reason: Section 2 is one incorporation entry point: it allows formation of an agricultural land owners association and issuance of letters of incorporation on a regulated application.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Formation application for agricultural land owners association

evidenceText: may be formed for the purposes of this Act and the regulations
Letters of incorporation forming an agricultural land owners association may be issued upon application

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections concern forming the association and obtaining letters of incorporation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how an agricultural land owners association may be formed and how letters of incorporation may be issued.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 3
proposals.reason: Section 3 is a coherent certificate workflow for approved applications, registration, issuance, and the conclusive evidence effect of the certificate.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Certificate as letters of incorporation

evidenceText: the Minister shall register the application for letters of incorporation
the Minister shall issue a certificate
shall constitute the letters of incorporation
shall be conclusive evidence

proposedGroups.reason: All three subsections explain how registration and certificate issuance create and prove incorporation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how an approved application is registered and how the Minister's certificate constitutes conclusive letters of incorporation.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 4
proposals.reason: Section 4 is one purposes provision listing what an agricultural land owners association exists to promote, facilitate, provide, manage, and carry out.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Objects and purposes of agricultural land owners association

evidenceText: promote and facilitate the stewardship, protection and improvement of agricultural land
facilitate the provision and distribution of water sources and supply systems for irrigation
facilitate and provide for the drainage of agricultural land
such other activities or duties as may be authorized or required

proposedGroups.reason: The listed paragraphs are the association's purpose statement and are best learned together.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the stewardship, irrigation, drainage, and authorized-duty purposes of an agricultural land owners association.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 5
proposals.reason: Section 5 is a single capacity rule giving an agricultural land owners association natural-person powers for its objects and purposes, subject to the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Natural-person powers of agricultural land owners association

evidenceText: has the capacity and, subject to this Act, the rights, powers and privileges of a natural person

proposedGroups.reason: The whole section states one legal capacity rule.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that an agricultural land owners association has natural-person rights, powers, and privileges for its objects and purposes, subject to the Act.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 6
proposals.reason: Section 6 is one by-law topic covering the association's by-law power and the non-application of the Regulations Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Association by-laws and Regulations Act exclusion

evidenceText: may make by-laws for the control and management
The Regulations Act does not apply to a by-law

proposedGroups.reason: The two subsections define the by-law authority and its statutory treatment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the association's by-law authority and that the Regulations Act does not apply to those by-laws.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 7
proposals.reason: Section 7 is a unified advisory-functions provision naming who the association may advise and the agricultural land, management practice, land use law, and Act-related topics of that advice.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Advisory functions of agricultural land owners association

evidenceText: advise a local government on the installation of facilities or services
advise the Minister and local government on acceptable management practices
advise local government on matters relating to land use laws
advise the Minister on matters relating to this Act

proposedGroups.reason: The paragraphs together define the association's advisory role.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who an agricultural land owners association may advise and the subjects covered by its advisory functions.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 8
proposals.reason: Section 8 is one registry duty for the Minister, with a repealed paragraph that should not be a separate study focus.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister's agricultural land registry duties

evidenceText: establish and maintain a registry of agricultural lands
register agricultural lands and remove agricultural lands from the registry

proposedGroups.reason: The current paragraphs state the Minister's registry duties for agricultural land.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the Minister must maintain the agricultural lands registry and register or remove agricultural lands in accordance with the regulations.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 9
proposals.reason: Section 9 is a single application rule allowing a person to apply to register agricultural land owned by that person.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Application to register owned agricultural land

evidenceText: make application to register agricultural land owned by the person

proposedGroups.reason: The section contains one permission to apply for registration of the applicant's own agricultural land.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who may apply to register agricultural land and that the application must be made in accordance with the regulations.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 10
proposals.reason: The target contains only a repealed registered agricultural land provision and no current operative rule to study.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 11
proposals.reason: Section 11 is one recommendation power tied to unregistered land the Minister considers suitable as agricultural land and possible inclusion in a land use control law.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister recommendation for unregistered suitable agricultural land

evidenceText: may recommend to the Minister of Local Government or a local government
agricultural land that is not registered under section 8
be considered for inclusion in the appropriate land use control law

proposedGroups.reason: The section states when and to whom the Minister may recommend consideration under a land use control law.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the Minister may recommend unregistered but suitable agricultural land for consideration in the appropriate land use control law.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 12
proposals.reason: Section 12 contains distinct construction topics: applying to build a ditch or drain through adjacent property, deposit-based permission and payouts, and the Minister's investigation, construction, and assessment powers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Application to construct ditch or drain through adjacent property

evidenceText: necessary for the proper drainage of agricultural land
run a ditch or drain through the property of an adjacent owner
may apply to the Minister for permission

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 12(1) states when an owner or association may seek permission to construct across adjacent property.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an owner or agricultural land owners association may apply to construct a ditch or drain through an adjacent owner's property.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Deposit condition and permission to construct ditch or drain

evidenceText: deposits with the Minister an amount of money
sufficient to cover all damages
the Minister may grant the applicant permission
shall pay out the sum so deposited

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 12(2) covers the deposit required for damages and investigation expenses, permission, and payout.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a deposit supports permission to construct a ditch or drain and payment to entitled persons.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister powers for ditch or drain construction

evidenceText: investigate the need for the ditch or drain
estimate the cost of the ditch or drain
attempt to seek an agreement among the interested parties
construct the ditch or drain whether or not the Minister obtains an agreement
assess each owner of the benefited land

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 12(3) lists the Minister's supporting powers for construction applications.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the investigation, agreement, construction, and cost-assessment powers the Minister may use for ditch or drain construction.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 13
proposals.reason: Section 13 is one protective court-order provision for ditch or drain construction affecting land of minors, mentally incompetent persons, or non-residents.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court protection for minors, mentally incompetent persons, and non-residents

evidenceText: person entitled to land through which any ditch or drain is proposed to be constructed
is a minor, a mentally incompetent person or a non-resident of the Province
make an order for the service of the person or the protection of the person's interests

proposedGroups.reason: The section states who is protected and what order a judge may make on a construction application.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a judge may order service or protection of interests for a minor, mentally incompetent person, or non-resident affected by proposed ditch or drain construction.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 14
proposals.reason: Section 14 is a single prohibition on placing water-flow impediments in a jointly paid ditch or drain without consent of all served owners.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Consent required before placing impediment in shared drain

evidenceText: constructed to serve the property of two or more adjacent owners
jointly paid for by these owners
shall not place any impediment
without first obtaining the consent of all owners served

proposedGroups.reason: The whole section defines the shared-ditch or drain context and the consent requirement before placing an impediment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when owners of land traversed by a shared ditch or drain must obtain consent before placing an impediment that interferes with water passage.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 15
proposals.reason: Section 15 covers related but separable repair topics: joint maintenance responsibility, applications when mutual consent fails, deposit-based permission, and the Minister's repair powers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Joint responsibility for shared ditch or drain maintenance

evidenceText: constructed to serve the property of two or more adjacent owners
the owners shall be jointly responsible for the maintenance and repair

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 15(1) identifies when adjacent owners are jointly responsible for maintenance and repair.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when owners are jointly responsible for maintaining and repairing a ditch or drain on agricultural land.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Application and deposit for ditch or drain repair permission

evidenceText: repair cannot be carried out and financed by mutual consent
may apply to the Minister for permission to carry out the repair work
deposits with the Minister an amount of money
the Minister may grant the applicant permission to repair

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 15(2) and 15(3) cover when repair permission is sought and the deposit condition for permission and payout.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an association or agricultural land owners may apply for repair permission and how the deposit condition operates.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister powers for ditch or drain repair

evidenceText: investigate the need for the repair
estimate the cost of the repair
attempt to seek an agreement among the interested parties
carry out the repair of the ditch or drain whether or not the Minister obtains an agreement
assess each owner of the benefited land

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 15(4) separately lists the Minister's powers for repair work and cost assessment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the investigation, agreement, repair, and assessment powers the Minister may use for ditch or drain repair.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 16
proposals.reason: Section 16 is one review route for a person dissatisfied with damage amounts determined by the Minister under section 12 or 15.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Review of Minister-determined damage amount

evidenceText: not satisfied with the amount for damage as determined by the Minister
may refer the matter to The Court of King's Bench of New Brunswick
under Part II of the Expropriation Act

proposedGroups.reason: The section states the trigger for review and the court or judge to which the matter may be referred.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a person dissatisfied with a Minister-determined damage amount under section 12 or 15 may seek review.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 17
proposals.reason: Section 17 is one cost-recovery provision making assessed construction or repair costs a Crown debt recoverable by action, with court authority over action costs.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Crown debt and action costs for ditch or drain work

evidenceText: shall constitute a debt due to the Crown in right of the Province
may be recovered by action in the name of the Crown
The court may make an order as to the costs of such action

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address recovery of Minister-incurred construction or repair costs and court costs in the recovery action.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how assessed construction or repair costs become a Crown debt and how court costs may be ordered in the recovery action.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 18
proposals.reason: Section 18 is one offences provision for violating or failing to comply with regulations, including the default category B offence and substituted prescribed categories.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Offence categories for regulation violations

evidenceText: violates or fails to comply with any provision of the regulations commits an offence
punishable under Part II of the Provincial Offences Procedure Act as a category B offence
commits an offence of the category prescribed by regulation

proposedGroups.reason: The two subsections work together to define default and prescribed offence categories for regulation non-compliance.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the default category B offence for regulation violations and when a prescribed offence category applies instead.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 19
proposals.reason: Section 19 is a single administration provision assigning responsibility to the Minister and allowing designation of persons to act on the Minister's behalf.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister administration and designation authority

evidenceText: The Minister is responsible for the administration of this Act and the regulations
may designate persons to act on the Minister's behalf

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections identify who administers the Act and how others may act for the Minister.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Minister's responsibility for administration and the Minister's authority to designate persons to act on the Minister's behalf.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 20
proposals.reason: Section 20 is a regulation-making provision with distinct subject clusters for agricultural land and operations, association and registry administration, farm environmental and drainage matters, and offences, appeals, and definitions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulations for agricultural land suitability and operations

evidenceText: criteria for determining whether land that is not in use in an agricultural operation is suitable
prescribing an agricultural activity or process for the purposes of the definition "agricultural operation"

proposedGroups.reason: Paragraphs (a) and (a.1) address land suitability and activities included in agricultural operation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers for agricultural land suitability criteria and prescribed agricultural activities or processes.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulations for associations and agricultural land registry

evidenceText: application for and registry of letters of incorporation
revoking of letters patent
eligibility requirements for membership
establishment and maintenance of a registry of agricultural land
registration, including the application for registration, of agricultural land

proposedGroups.reason: These paragraphs concern incorporation, membership, letters patent, and the agricultural land registry.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers for association incorporation, membership, letters patent, and registration of agricultural land.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulations for manure, wastes, artificial topsoil, and drains

evidenceText: storage, handling and application of manure
disposal of agricultural wastes
manufacture of artificial topsoil
construction and maintenance of drains on agricultural land

proposedGroups.reason: These paragraphs cover farm-material handling and physical drain construction or maintenance.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers for manure, agricultural wastes, artificial topsoil, and agricultural land drains.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulations for offence categories, appeals, and definitions

evidenceText: prescribing, in relation to offences under the regulations, categories of offences
respecting appeals, including the designation of an appeal body
defining any word or expression used in this Act but not defined in this Act

proposedGroups.reason: The closing paragraphs authorize regulations for offence categories, appeals, and supplemental definitions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers for offence categories, appeals, appeal bodies, and defining otherwise undefined words or expressions.

Agricultural Land Protection

proposals.reason: The target contains only repealed consequential amendments and no current operative rule to study.

Section 1 defines the core Air Space Act concepts, with distinct terms for parcels and plans, vertical measurement, registry roles, and survey roles. The repealed geodetic elevation entry is not a study focus.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Air space parcel and air space plan definitions

evidenceText: a volumetric parcel of air space
created under section 3
a plan that complies with the requirements of sections 4 and 5

proposedGroups.reason: These definitions identify the Act's central parcel and plan concepts.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what an air space parcel is and what makes a plan an air space plan.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Orthometric height definition

evidenceText: the elevation of a point above the geoid
based on the Canadian Geodetic Vertical Datum of 2013
derived from a benchmark approved by the Director of Surveys

proposedGroups.reason: Orthometric height is a technical measurement definition used in air space plan requirements.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how orthometric height is defined for Air Space Act purposes.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Development officer, registry office, and registrar definitions

evidenceText: a development officer under the Community Planning Act
registry office established under the Registry Act
registrar of deeds of that county

proposedGroups.reason: These definitions identify the planning and registry officials and offices used by the Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who the development officer and registrar are and what registry office means.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Director of Surveys and surveyor definitions

evidenceText: Director of Surveys under the Surveys Act
a land surveyor registered under the New Brunswick Land Surveyors Act, 1986

proposedGroups.reason: These definitions identify the survey authority and professional actor named in the Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what Director of Surveys and surveyor mean in the Air Space Act.

proposals.reason: Section 2 is a single legal-status rule that air space constitutes land and may be dealt with as land.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Air space as land

evidenceText: Air space constitutes land and may be dealt with as land

proposedGroups.reason: The whole section states the core status and dealing rule for air space.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that air space constitutes land and may be dealt with as land.

proposals.reason: Section 3 is one creation rule allowing an owner of a freehold or leasehold estate to create air space parcels by filing an air space plan in the registry office.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Creation of air space parcel by filing plan

evidenceText: owner of a freehold or leasehold estate
by filing an air space plan in the registry office
create one or more air space parcels separated by surfaces

proposedGroups.reason: The section identifies who may create parcels, the filing method, and the separated-surface nature of the parcels.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a freehold or leasehold owner creates one or more air space parcels by filing an air space plan.

proposals.reason: Section 4 contains several technical requirements for air space plans. The requirements split naturally into land and boundary identification, height and limit requirements, and required plan drawings and dimensions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Land identification and side boundary requirements for air space plan

evidenceText: identify the parcel of land of which the air space parcel is part
indicate that the plan is a subdivision
side boundary limits consist of vertical or inclined surfaces

proposedGroups.reason: Paragraphs (a) and (b) describe how the plan ties the air space parcel to the underlying land and side boundaries.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how an air space plan must identify the parent land and show side boundary limits.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Upper, lower, and orthometric height requirements

evidenceText: as its upper and lower limit a horizontal or inclined plane or arc of a circle
noted on it the orthometric height of one corner
orthometric height of every corner or angle of the air space parcel

proposedGroups.reason: Paragraphs (c) and (d) focus on vertical limits and height notation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the upper and lower limit forms and orthometric height notations required on an air space plan.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Plot, paraline drawing, and dimension requirements

evidenceText: a plot to scale of the parcel of land
a three-dimensional paraline drawing of the air space parcel
all boundaries of the air space parcel shall be fully dimensioned for length and direction

proposedGroups.reason: Paragraph (e) and its closing clause state the drawing and dimension information the plan must include.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the plot, three-dimensional paraline drawing, statement, and dimension requirements for an air space plan.

proposals.reason: Section 5 has two filing acceptance topics: the ordinary certificate and approval prerequisites, and the added development officer certification requirement when subdivision controls affect the land.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Surveyor, development officer, and Director approvals before filing

evidenceText: shall not be accepted by the registrar for filing unless
certificate and seal of a surveyor
approved by a development officer
approved by the Director of Surveys

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 5(1) lists the ordinary prerequisites before the registrar may accept an air space plan for filing.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the surveyor certification and approvals required before an air space plan can be accepted for filing.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Subdivision-control certification before filing

evidenceText: affected by a subdivision by-law or subdivision regulation
shall not be accepted by the registrar for filing unless a development officer has certified
requirements of subsection 79(3) or paragraph 125(11)(c) of the Community Planning Act have been met

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 5(2) adds a separate filing condition for land affected by subdivision controls.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when subdivision by-law or regulation status requires development officer certification before an air space plan is accepted for filing.

proposals.reason: Section 6 is one conveyance and title-effect topic for air space parcels, including how they may be dealt with, what is not implied, and what air space remains with the transferor unless conveyed.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Conveyance and retained title for air space parcel

evidenceText: may be conveyed or otherwise dealt with in the same manner and form as other land
does not convey an easement of any kind
title to the air space above the upper limits and below the lower limits of an air space parcel remains in the transferor

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections work together to state how air space parcels are conveyed and what interests are excluded or retained.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how an air space parcel may be conveyed, what a conveyance does not imply, and what title remains with the transferor unless expressly conveyed.

proposals.reason: Section 7 is a single assessment and taxation rule for separately owned air space parcels.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Air space parcel as real property for assessment and taxation

evidenceText: if separately owned, constitutes real property for the purposes of assessment and taxation

proposedGroups.reason: The whole section states the real-property status of separately owned air space parcels for assessment and taxation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that a separately owned air space parcel constitutes real property for assessment and taxation.

proposals.reason: Section 7.1 is one administration rule assigning responsibility for the Act to Service New Brunswick.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Service New Brunswick administration of Air Space Act

evidenceText: Service New Brunswick is responsible for the administration of this Act

proposedGroups.reason: The section contains a single administrative responsibility statement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that Service New Brunswick is responsible for administration of the Air Space Act.

proposals.reason: Section 8 is one regulation-making authority for Director of Surveys regulations about survey standards and air space plan content.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Director of Surveys regulation power for air space plans

evidenceText: The Director of Surveys may make regulations
standards of survey
content of an air space plan

proposedGroups.reason: The section states the regulator and the two subjects that may be regulated.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the Director of Surveys may regulate survey standards and the content of an air space plan.

proposals.reason: Section 1 is a large definitions section. The target supports separate groups for aquaculture activity and products, aquaculture land and management designations, named institutions, and operational health terms.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Aquaculture activity, product, organism, and farming definitions

evidenceText: the farming of aquatic organisms for commercial or scientific purposes
aquatic organism raised or being raised by aquaculture
plants, algae and animals that have water as their natural habitat
intervention in the rearing of aquatic organisms

proposedGroups.reason: These definitions explain the aquaculture activity and organisms covered by the Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the definitions for aquaculture, aquaculture product, aquatic organisms, and farming.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Aquaculture land, legislation, and management area definitions

evidenceText: land that is designated by the Minister as aquaculture land under section 8
a statute, regulation or statutory instrument relating to fisheries or aquaculture
an area designated by the Minister as an aquaculture management area under section 7

proposedGroups.reason: These definitions identify designated aquaculture places and the prescribed legal instruments relating to fisheries or aquaculture.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the definitions for aquaculture land, aquaculture legislation, and aquaculture management area.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Appeal Board, Chief Veterinary Officer, and Department definitions

evidenceText: Licensing and Penalty Appeal Board established under section 59 of the Seafood Processing Act
person appointed as Chief Veterinary Officer under section 54
Department of Agriculture, Aquaculture and Fisheries

proposedGroups.reason: These definitions identify the board, officer, and department named in the Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the definitions for Appeal Board, Chief Veterinary Officer, and Department.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Equipment, fallow period, and fish health diagnostic service definitions

evidenceText: tools and materials used in the conduct of aquaculture
period of time during which aquaculture products shall not be present
laboratory that is approved by the Chief Veterinary Officer

proposedGroups.reason: These definitions cover operational materials, fallow periods, and approved diagnostic laboratories.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the definitions for equipment, fallow period, and fish health diagnostic service.

proposals.reason: Section 2 is one application provision stating the Act's general application to aquaculture, regulation-based exemptions, and the duty of exempted persons to comply with prescribed terms and conditions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Application of Aquaculture Act and regulation-based exemptions

evidenceText: this Act applies to all aquaculture in the Province
When exempted from the application of this Act by the regulations
a person or class of persons
land or a class of lands
aquatic organisms or a class of aquatic organisms
shall comply with any terms and conditions prescribed by regulation

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections work together to define general application, exemption categories, and continuing prescribed conditions for exempted persons.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Aquaculture Act's general application, the categories that may be exempted by regulation, and the terms and conditions that exempted persons must follow.

proposals.reason: The target states a single interpretive protection preserving existing aboriginal or treaty rights from being abrogated or derogated by the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Aquaculture Act s. 3: Existing aboriginal or treaty rights

evidenceText: nothing in this Act shall be construed so as to abrogate or derogate from the protection provided for the existing aboriginal or treaty rights

proposedGroups.reason: The full section is one coherent rights-preservation rule.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that Aquaculture Act section 3 preserves existing aboriginal or treaty rights from abrogation or derogation by the Act.

proposals.reason: The section is one learning topic about the Minister's agreement-making authority for administering the Act, including intergovernmental programs and committees.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Aquaculture Act s. 4: Minister agreements for administration
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 4(1) and 4(2) together describe when the Minister may enter agreements and what agreement-related arrangements may be made.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Minister's authority under Aquaculture Act section 4 to enter agreements and establish agreement-related committees for aquaculture administration.

proposals.reason: The target contains separate recall topics for creating advisory committees, their advisory function, and member remuneration and expenses.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Aquaculture Act s. 5: Establishing advisory committees
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 5(1) to 5(4) address committee establishment, membership, chair designation, and meetings.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how advisory committees are established, appointed, chaired, and called to meet under Aquaculture Act section 5.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Aquaculture Act s. 5: Advisory committee consultation
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 5(5) separately states the consultative and advisory role of a committee when requested by the Minister.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an advisory committee consults with and advises the Minister on aquaculture matters.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Aquaculture Act s. 5: Committee allowance and expenses
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 5(6) and 5(7) focus on service without salary, possible allowances, and reimbursement of expenses.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the salary, allowance, and expense rules for members of advisory committees under Aquaculture Act section 5.

proposals.reason: The section is a coherent topic on Minister-established aquaculture policies, standards, procedures, and guidelines, including publication and Regulations Act treatment.

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 53(1) prohibits selling, destroying, or otherwise disposing of aquaculture products in which hazards are or may be present.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize the prohibition on selling, destroying, or disposing of aquaculture products that contain or may contain hazards.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Transfer or transport of live aquaculture products
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 53(2) separately prohibits transfer or transport of live aquaculture products between bodies of water or sites except in accordance with regulations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when live aquaculture products may be transferred or transported from one body of water or site to another.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Introducing live aquaculture products
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 53(3) separately prohibits introducing live aquaculture products to a body of water or site except in accordance with regulations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the rule for introducing live aquaculture products to a body of water or site.

proposals.reason: Section 54 covers the Chief Veterinary Officer's appointment and role, information access and sharing powers, and designation of persons to act on the officer's behalf.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Chief Veterinary Officer appointment and duties
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 54(1) and 54(2) establish appointment of the Chief Veterinary Officer and the officer's powers and duties under the Act and regulations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Describe who appoints the Chief Veterinary Officer and the officer's general powers and duties.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Chief Veterinary Officer information powers
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 54(3) and 54(4) address database access and collection or disclosure of prescribed information, including personal information.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain the Chief Veterinary Officer's access, collection, and disclosure powers for prescribed information.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Chief Veterinary Officer designation
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 54(5) separately allows the Chief Veterinary Officer to designate persons to act on the officer's behalf.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the Chief Veterinary Officer may designate one or more persons to act on the officer's behalf.

proposals.reason: Section 55 divides into approval authority and application mechanics, and then terms and conditions with a compliance duty.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Chief Veterinary Officer approvals
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 55(1) and 55(2) state when written approval may allow prescribed activity and what an approval application must include.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Describe the Chief Veterinary Officer's written approval power and the form, fee, and information requirements for applying.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Approval terms and conditions
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 55(3) and 55(4) address the terms and conditions attached to approvals and the recipient's duty to comply.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that approvals may be subject to terms and conditions and that the approved person must comply with them.

proposals.reason: Section 56 contains distinct containment and property rules, plus separate duties to report and respond to containment structure failures.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Containment and property of aquaculture products
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 56(1) and 56(2) pair the licence holder's containment duty with the personal property status of products contained within the licensed site.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain the licence holder's containment duty and when specified aquaculture products are the licence holder's exclusive personal property.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Containment structure failures
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 56(3) and 56(4) focus on reporting a containment structure failure and taking prescribed measures after a failure.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the licence holder's reporting and response duties when a site's containment structures fail.

proposals.reason: Section 57 states one Ministerial duty to establish a regulatory list of reportable conditions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: List of reportable conditions

evidenceText: The Minister shall, by regulation, establish a list of reportable conditions.

proposedGroups.reason: The target contains a single rule requiring the Minister to establish the list of reportable conditions by regulation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the Minister must establish the list of reportable conditions by regulation.

proposals.reason: Section 58 is a focused order power allowing the Chief Veterinary Officer to declare an unprescribed hazard to be a reportable condition when an aquaculture health emergency exists or may exist.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Declaration of reportable condition

evidenceText: the Chief Veterinary Officer may make an order declaring the hazard to be a reportable condition.

proposedGroups.reason: The provision states the emergency opinion trigger and the Chief Veterinary Officer's power to declare a hazard as a reportable condition by order.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain when the Chief Veterinary Officer may order that an unprescribed hazard be treated as a reportable condition.

proposals.reason: Section 59 separates the definition of a mortality event, the duty to report reportable conditions or mortality events, and the requirement that reports be made according to regulations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mortality event at a site
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 59(1) defines when a mortality event has occurred at a site by reference to unexpected deaths and prescribed classes, periods, rates, numbers, proportions, or circumstances.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when a mortality event has occurred at a site for the purposes of the reporting provision.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Reporting reportable conditions and mortality events
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 59(2) identifies who must report and the reasonable-grounds triggers for reporting a reportable condition or mortality event.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Describe who must report and what beliefs trigger the duty to report a reportable condition or mortality event.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Report made in accordance with regulations
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 59(3) separately states that reports under subsection 59(2) must be made in accordance with regulations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that a report of a reportable condition or mortality event must be made in accordance with the regulations.

proposals.reason: Section 60 states a single prohibition against knowingly providing or attempting to provide false or misleading information to the Chief Veterinary Officer in approval applications or reports.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: False or misleading information to Chief Veterinary Officer

evidenceText: No person who applies for an approval or makes a report shall knowingly provide, or attempt to provide, false or misleading information to the Chief Veterinary Officer.

proposedGroups.reason: The provision focuses on false or misleading information connected to approval applications and reports made to the Chief Veterinary Officer.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize the prohibition on knowingly providing or attempting to provide false or misleading information to the Chief Veterinary Officer.

proposals.reason: Section 61 states one protection from proceedings for good-faith reports about reportable conditions made in accordance with the Act or regulations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Protection for good-faith reports

evidenceText: No action or other proceeding shall be instituted against a person who, in good faith, makes a report in respect of a reportable condition

proposedGroups.reason: The target provides a single liability protection for a person who makes a good-faith report in respect of a reportable condition in accordance with the Act or regulations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a person is protected from action or other proceedings for making a report about a reportable condition.

proposals.reason: Section 62 is a coherent list of discretionary Chief Veterinary Officer powers in response to alleged or actual reportable conditions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Chief Veterinary Officer powers for reportable conditions

evidenceText: The Chief Veterinary Officer may, in his or her discretion,

proposedGroups.reason: The provision lists related discretionary powers to direct investigations, cause tests or scientific investigations, and take suppression, limitation, or treatment measures.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the Chief Veterinary Officer's discretionary investigation, testing, and response powers for reportable conditions.

proposals.reason: Section 63 is a unified reportable-condition order provision covering the order power, compliance time, and possible quarantine, destruction, or disposal requirements.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Order respecting reportable condition
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections work together to describe orders directing action or inaction for suppression, limitation, or treatment of reportable conditions, including timing and quarantine, destruction, or disposal requirements.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain what an order respecting a reportable condition may direct, including compliance timing and quarantine, destruction, or disposal of aquaculture products.

proposals.reason: Section 64 is a coherent designation provision for controlled aquaculture areas, including amendment, cancellation, reinstatement, and exclusion of the Regulations Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Controlled aquaculture area designation
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections together state when a site and surrounding area may be designated as a controlled aquaculture area and how that designation may change or be treated procedurally.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Describe when the Chief Veterinary Officer may designate a controlled aquaculture area and what rules apply to changing or treating that designation.

proposals.reason: Section 65 states a single order power over licence holders whose sites are in controlled aquaculture areas to prevent the spread of hazards.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Measures in controlled aquaculture area

evidenceText: directing a licence holder whose site is located in a controlled aquaculture area to take any measures considered necessary to prevent the spread of hazards

proposedGroups.reason: The target focuses on the Chief Veterinary Officer's power to direct necessary hazard-prevention measures, including quarantine, destruction, or disposal of aquaculture products.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain what measures the Chief Veterinary Officer may order a licence holder to take in a controlled aquaculture area to prevent the spread of hazards.

proposals.reason: Section 66 is a focused appeal provision for orders of the Chief Veterinary Officer made under the Part and the effect of an appeal on the order.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Chief Veterinary Officer order appeals
proposedGroups.reason: The two subsections identify the right to appeal Chief Veterinary Officer orders under the Part and state that the appeal does not stay the decision unless the officer directs otherwise.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain who may appeal an order of the Chief Veterinary Officer and whether the appeal stays the order.

proposals.reason: Section 67 is a coherent inspector appointment and identification provision.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Inspector appointment and certificate
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections address appointment or designation of inspectors, issuance of certificates, and production of the certificate on request.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Describe how inspectors are appointed or designated and what certificate duties apply to inspectors.

proposals.reason: Section 68 contains a broad inspection power, special rules for warrants and dwelling entry, and a separate power to request peace officer assistance.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Inspection powers for compliance
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 68(1) lists the inspector's powers at reasonable times for ensuring compliance with the Act and regulations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the places, materials, inquiries, tests, assistance, and incidental powers available to an inspector during a compliance inspection.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Entry warrants and private dwellings
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 68(2) and 68(3) specifically address applying for entry warrants and the conditions for entering a private dwelling.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain when an inspector may seek an entry warrant and when a private dwelling may be entered for an inspection.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Peace officer assistance
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 68(4) separately authorizes an inspector acting under the section to request peace officer assistance.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that an inspector acting under section 68 may request the assistance of a peace officer.

proposals.reason: Section 69 separates the handling of removed books, records, or documents from the evidentiary effect of certified copies or extracts.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Removing books records or documents
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 69(1) and 69(2) address when an inspector may remove records for copying or extracts and the receipt and prompt return duties that follow.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain when an inspector may remove books, records, or documents and what receipt and return duties apply.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Certified copies and extracts as evidence
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 69(3) separately gives certified copies or extracts the same admissibility and evidentiary value as the originals.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the evidentiary value of certified copies or extracts from removed books, records, or documents.

proposals.reason: Section 70 is a focused samples-and-tests provision requiring fish health diagnostic service testing and notice of results to the Chief Veterinary Officer.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Fish health diagnostic service tests
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections together require specified tests to be performed by a fish health diagnostic service and require immediate notice of test results to the Chief Veterinary Officer.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who must perform required tests and when test results must be given to the Chief Veterinary Officer.

proposals.reason: Section 71 contains distinct seizure authority, post-seizure detention or removal rules, and sale or return/payment consequences for seized items.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Seizure of evidence of an offence
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 71(1) states what an inspector may seize, the reasonable-grounds evidence threshold, and the circumstances in which seizure may occur.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify what may be seized as evidence of an offence and the circumstances in which an inspector may seize it.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Detention after seizure
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 71(2) and 71(3) govern where seized items may be detained or removed and how long detention may last depending on whether a prosecution begins.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how seized items may be detained or removed and the time limits on detention after seizure.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Sale return or payment after seizure
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 71(4) and 71(5) address sale of seized aquatic organisms and the return of seized items or payment for sold organisms when proceedings are not taken or the person is acquitted.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Describe when seized aquatic organisms may be sold and what return or payment obligations apply if no proceedings follow or the charge ends in acquittal.

proposals.reason: Section 72 is a coherent obstruction provision covering interference with inspectors and false or misleading statements to inspectors.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Obstruction and false statements to inspector
proposedGroups.reason: The two subsections prohibit obstructing or interfering with an inspector and knowingly making false or misleading statements to an inspector carrying out or attempting an inspection.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize the prohibitions on obstructing an inspector and knowingly making false or misleading statements to an inspector.

proposals.reason: Section 73 covers several distinct offence-and-penalty topics: Act offences linked to Schedule A, minimum and continuing fines, prosecution timing, and regulation offences with prescribed categories.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Act offences listed in Schedule A
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 73(1) and 73(2) establish offences for violating listed Act provisions and connect each listed provision to the Schedule A offence category.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how violations of Act provisions listed in Schedule A become offences and how their categories are assigned.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minimum fines and continuing offences
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 73(3) and 73(4) set minimum fines for specified offence categories and calculate minimum and maximum fines when an offence continues for more than one day.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the category-specific minimum fines and how fines are multiplied for continuing offences.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Time limit for prosecutions
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 73(5) separately states the two-year period for commencing a prosecution for an offence under the Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the two-year time limit for commencing a prosecution for an offence under the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulation offences and categories
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 73(6) and 73(7) address offences for violating regulations and the offence category when a category has been prescribed by regulation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain when violating or failing to comply with a regulation is an offence and how a prescribed category applies.

proposals.reason: Section 74 separates the judge's available additional orders after conviction from the effective-date and maximum-duration rules for those orders.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Judicial orders after conviction
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 74(1) lists the types of orders a judge may make in addition to other penalties after considering the offence and its circumstances.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the kinds of orders a judge may make in addition to other penalties after a conviction under the Act or regulations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Effective date and duration of judicial orders
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 74(2) and 74(3) state when an order takes effect and require the judge to specify a period that does not exceed five years.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a judicial order takes effect and the maximum period for which it may remain in effect.

proposals.reason: Section 75 states the Minister may recover specific aquatic-organism costs for seizure, care, disposal, risk reduction, and health or welfare preservation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister recovery of aquatic organism costs

evidenceText: the costs incurred in the seizure, housing, keeping, maintaining, disposal or destruction of an aquatic organism
the costs of eliminating or reducing the risk
the costs of preserving the health or welfare

proposedGroups.reason: The section is a focused cost-recovery power listing the aquatic-organism costs the Minister may recover.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the aquatic-organism seizure, care, disposal, risk-reduction, and health or welfare costs the Minister may recover.

proposals.reason: Section 76 gives the Minister a specific power to charge interest on amounts owing under the Act or regulations at a prescribed or calculated rate.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister interest on amounts owing

evidenceText: The Minister may charge interest on an amount owing to the Minister
at a rate prescribed by regulation or at a rate calculated in the manner prescribed by regulation

proposedGroups.reason: The section is a single interest-charging rule for amounts owing to the Minister.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister may charge interest on amounts owing and how the interest rate is set.

proposals.reason: Section 77 contains two study topics: certificate-based debt enforcement for amounts owing and separate joint and several liability for directors of corporate debtors.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Debt certificate filing and enforcement

evidenceText: constitutes a debt due to the Province
may issue a certificate stating the amount of the debt due
may be filed in The Court of King’s Bench of New Brunswick
All reasonable costs and charges

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 77(1) through 77(4) explain how an amount owing becomes a debt, how the Minister may certify it, and how the filed certificate and costs may be enforced.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how an amount owing becomes a debt due to the Province and how a Minister certificate may be filed, enforced, and include related costs.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Corporate debtor director liability

evidenceText: When a debtor is a corporation
the directors of the corporation
are jointly and severally liable

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 77(5) separately assigns joint and several liability to directors when a corporate debtor fails to pay an amount due and payable.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when directors of a corporate debtor are jointly and severally liable for the amount due, interest, and penalties.

proposals.reason: Section 78 is a coherent forfeiture provision for aquatic organisms and other seized things following conviction, including the effect of an order and the relationship to other penalties.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Forfeiture of seized aquatic organisms and other things

evidenceText: is forfeited to the Minister on the conviction
the judge may order any other thing seized
the thing seized is forfeited to the Minister
in addition to any other penalty

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections work together to describe automatic forfeiture, judge-ordered forfeiture, and how forfeiture relates to penalties.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what property may be forfeited after conviction and that forfeiture is additional to any other penalty.

proposals.reason: Section 79 gives connected rules for delivering seized aquatic organisms and disposing of forfeited equipment or other things.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Disposal of seized or forfeited property

evidenceText: deliver it to the Minister
shall deal with it in accordance with the instructions of the Minister
not sooner than 30 days after conviction

proposedGroups.reason: The section focuses on what inspectors and the Minister do with seized aquatic organisms and forfeited equipment or other things.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who handles seized aquatic organisms and forfeited things, and when the Minister may dispose of equipment or another thing after conviction.

proposals.reason: Section 80 states when an inspector must return seized property other than equipment or an aquatic organism.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Return of seized things after no charge or no forfeiture

evidenceText: shall return it to the owner or person in possession
as soon as the circumstances permit
within 30 days after the final disposition of the charge

proposedGroups.reason: The section is a focused return rule for seized things outside equipment and aquatic organisms, with separate timing for no charge and charge outcomes.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an inspector must return a seized thing because no charge is laid, no conviction results, or no forfeiture is ordered.

proposals.reason: Section 81 states what may happen to seized property when lawful ownership or entitlement cannot be ascertained within three months.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Forfeiture when ownership is not ascertainable

evidenceText: lawful ownership or entitlement to it cannot be ascertained within three months after the seizure
may direct that it be disposed of
are forfeited to the Crown

proposedGroups.reason: The section is a single rule for disposal and Crown forfeiture when ownership or entitlement cannot be found within three months.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the three-month ownership trigger for Minister-directed disposal and forfeiture to the Crown.

proposals.reason: Section 82 is short but substantive: it allows the owner of a seized thing to abandon it to the Crown.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Owner abandonment of a seized thing

evidenceText: The owner of a seized thing may abandon it to the Crown

proposedGroups.reason: The target contains one direct permission for an owner to abandon seized property to the Crown.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the owner of a seized thing may abandon it to the Crown.

proposals.reason: Section 83 bars claims to indemnity or compensation for seizure, forfeiture, disposal, or destruction under the specified legislation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: No indemnity for seizure, forfeiture, disposal, or destruction

evidenceText: No person shall be entitled to, or have any claim or right to, any indemnity or compensation
in relation to a seizure, forfeiture, disposal or destruction

proposedGroups.reason: The section is a focused no-compensation rule tied to seizure, forfeiture, disposal, and destruction.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that no person has an indemnity or compensation claim for seizure, forfeiture, disposal, or destruction under the named Acts.

proposals.reason: Section 84 covers several order topics: general order status and amendment, publication and notice, service and compliance, duration, and finality.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Order status, limits, amendment, and non-delegation

evidenceText: the Regulations Act does not apply
may be limited as to time or place
may amend or revoke an order
shall not delegate the power to make an order

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 84(1) through 84(4) set the basic legal status of orders, time or place limits, amendment or revocation, and non-delegation for specified order powers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how orders are treated outside the Regulations Act, how they may be limited or changed, and which Minister order powers cannot be delegated.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Publication, effectiveness, validity, and notice of orders

evidenceText: is effective on the date it is made

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 84(5) through 84(10) state when orders are effective, which orders are published, and the effects of publication or failure to publish.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the publication, effective-date, validity, and notice rules for Minister and Chief Veterinary Officer orders.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Service, compliance, duration, and finality of orders

evidenceText: shall be in writing and shall be served
shall comply with the order within the time
remains in effect until revoked
is final and conclusive

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 84(11) through 84(14) address served orders, compliance duties, continuing effect until revocation, and limits on court review.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when orders must be served, when they must be complied with, how long they remain effective, and the limited grounds for review.

proposals.reason: Section 85 authorizes remedial orders and direct action for noncompliance, and makes resulting costs a debt due to the Province.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Remedial action and cost liability for order noncompliance

evidenceText: may order the taking of any remedial action considered necessary
fails or refuses to comply
may enter any place, area or vehicle except a dwelling house
becomes a debt due to the Province

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections together describe further remedial action, entry and action to effect compliance, and liability for resulting costs.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what remedial action may be ordered, what powers arise after noncompliance, and who is liable for resulting costs as a debt due to the Province.

proposals.reason: Section 86 provides an evidentiary rule for certified copies of remedial-action orders.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Certified copy evidence of remedial orders

evidenceText: A certified copy of an order referred to in subsection 85(1) may be entered in evidence
is, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, proof of the making of the order

proposedGroups.reason: The section is a single evidence rule for certified copies of orders referred to in subsection 85(1).
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what a certified copy of a subsection 85(1) order proves when entered in evidence.

proposals.reason: Section 87 links service and proof of service for orders to the relevant provisions of the Provincial Offences Procedure Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Service and proof of service of orders

evidenceText: An order that is to be served on a person under this Act may be served
service may be proved
in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Provincial Offences Procedure Act

proposedGroups.reason: The section is a focused rule for serving orders and proving that service.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that service and proof of service for orders follow the relevant Provincial Offences Procedure Act provisions.

proposals.reason: Section 88 provides immunity from proceedings for listed officials and authorized or engaged persons for good-faith acts or omissions under the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Good faith immunity for administration and enforcement

evidenceText: No action, application or other proceeding lies
in relation to anything done or purported to be done in good faith
or in relation to anything omitted in good faith

proposedGroups.reason: The section is a single immunity rule for good-faith administration and enforcement activity.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who receives immunity and that it covers good-faith acts or omissions under the Act.

proposals.reason: Section 89 assigns administration of the Act to the Minister and allows the Minister to designate persons to act on the Minister’s behalf.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister administration and designations

evidenceText: The Minister is responsible for the administration of this Act
may designate one or more persons to act on the Minister’s behalf

proposedGroups.reason: The section is a focused administration and designation rule.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the Minister administers the Act and may designate persons to act on the Minister’s behalf.

proposals.reason: Section 90 is a broad regulation-making provision with separable subjects for administration and licensing, health and containment, enforcement and forms, and general regulation mechanics.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulations for aquaculture legislation, exemptions, management areas, fees, and licences

exempting any person, land, site, aquatic organism or activity

prescribing application fees
establishing categories of licences

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulations for aquatic organisms, health, harvesting, transfer, containment, and reportable conditions

evidenceText: establishing conditions for the possession of live aquatic organisms
prescribing health, welfare, genetic and grade standards
respecting the harvesting of aquaculture products
respecting the transfer or transport of live aquaculture products
prescribing standards for the containment of aquaculture products

proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers for live aquatic organisms, aquaculture product standards, harvesting, transfer, introduction, containment, reporting, reportable conditions, and analysis methods.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulations for inspectors, offences, interest, forms, reports, and definitions

prescribing, in respect of offences under the regulations, categories of offences
prescribing an interest rate

proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers for inspectors, offence categories, interest rates, forms, reports, undefined expressions, and matters needed to carry out the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Incorporation, variation, and application of regulations

evidenceText: may incorporate by reference

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 90(2) through 90(4) state how regulations may incorporate external material, vary among classes, and be general, particular, time-limited, place-limited, or place-excluding.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how regulations may incorporate codes or standards, vary across persons or things, and be limited or general in application.

proposals.reason: Section 91 preserves existing aquaculture leases, occupation permits, licences, directions, approvals, and bay management area designations under the new Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Continuing validity of existing aquaculture instruments and area orders

evidenceText: shall be deemed to be a lease, permit or licence granted or issued
is valid until it expires
shall be deemed to be an order designating an aquaculture management area

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections are continuity rules for instruments and area orders that were in force immediately before commencement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how existing aquaculture instruments and bay management area orders continue or are deemed under the new Act.

proposals.reason: Section 92 is a coherent ongoing-hearings transition rule for appeals that were already underway before commencement.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ongoing hearings and deemed Appeal Board decisions

evidenceText: a decision of the Registrar was under appeal
the Minister shall complete the hearing
shall be completed in accordance with the law as it existed
shall be deemed to be a decision of the Appeal Board

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections together explain who completes ongoing hearings, which law applies, and how Minister decisions are treated as Appeal Board decisions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how ongoing Registrar appeal hearings are completed after commencement and when Minister decisions are deemed Appeal Board decisions.

proposals.reason: Section 93 makes consequential Seafood Processing Act amendments with separable topics: Appeal Board powers, new appeal rights, and regulation-making authority for Aquaculture Act appeals.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Appeal Board powers under the Seafood Processing Act

evidenceText: The Appeal Board may exercise any power conferred on the Appeal Board
